topic: MIDI port-number routing collision hijacks controller-to-server SysEx in FL 21.2.2
affected_file_api: fl_controller/FLStudioMCP/device_FLStudioMCP.py (OnIdle heartbeat, device.midiOutSysex); FL Studio Options > MIDI settings
context: After a clean FL restart with correct 'init ok' + '[FLStudioMCP] Ready' banner and no warnings, the daemon received zero heartbeats; both loopMIDI ports existed exactly once.
observation: The OUTPUT row 'FLStudioMCP RX' also carried Port 42 (same as 'FLStudioMCP TX'). Raw loopMIDI taps showed valid heartbeat SysEx (dir=3, MCP magic, 2/sec per HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL=0.5) arriving on the RX loopback instead of TX. midiOutSysex selects an output row by port number and matched RX first.
tested_values: Output FLStudioMCP RX Port 42 -> 10 (unique); TX output stays 42; RX input enabled with controller FLStudioMCP on 42; script reloaded.
result: fl_ping alive=true, heartbeat_age 0.28s; all four read-only gate tools returned live data on first call.
source_method: Raw mido taps on both loopMIDI ports decoded via fl_studio_mcp.protocol, then end-to-end MCP calls through the registered Hermes flstudio server.
reproduction_steps: Give two FL OUTPUT rows the same Port number, one named like the controller RX; heartbeats vanish from TX and appear on the RX loopback input.
known_pitfalls: The controller port number (42) must appear EXACTLY ONCE in the FL Output section, on FLStudioMCP TX, matching the controller INPUT row number.
FL 21.2.2 MIDI settings lists Outputs ABOVE Inputs; table confusion is common.
MIDI bindings are not persisted reliably across FL restarts: recheck input enable, controller assignment, and port numbers after every restart.
A 'Ready' banner proves neither routing nor daemon pairing; prove pairing via heartbeat age on the wire.
open_questions: Why FL 21.2.2 assigned the RX output row 42 on that restart (auto-numbering vs leftover state) is untested.
next_recommended_action: Add startup checklist (input row enabled + controller assigned + unique output port number) to agent onboarding docs; consider daemon-side alert when heartbeats are absent >30s.
